![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14255499/assets/40b6988e1f0c7e3b3cda0c077bafbedba95f5c83fce6fb1d0ee71ce34ecb1963.png)

We need to create a cylindrical tin with no lid using $108\pi \,{in}^{2}$ of sheet metal. What is the largest possible volume ${V}_{\text{max}}$ of the cylinder? Do not round the answer.

${V}_{\text{max}}=$
{{field-1}} ${\text{in}}^{3}$
question.worked_solution:
First, let $r$ be the radius and $h$ be the height of the cylinder.

We wish to maximize the volume

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

We know that the surface area is fixed at $108\pi \,{in}^{2},$ so we also have the constraint equation

$$
2\pi rh+\pi {r}^{2}=108\pi .
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi rh & =108\pi -\pi {r}^{2} \\ h & =\frac{54}{r}-\frac{r}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $V,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}V(r) & =\pi {r}^{2}(\frac{54}{r}-\frac{r}{2}) \\ V(r) & =(54r-\frac{{r}^{3}}{2})\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We want to maximize $V,$ so we need to differentiate $V$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{V}^{′}(r)=(54-\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2})\pi .
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ (54-\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2})\pi  & =0 \\ 54 & =\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =36 \\ r & =6\,\text{in}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that, in the last step, we only considered the positive root because the radius $r$ must be positive.

Finally, we confirm that $r=6$ is a maximum using the second derivative test. The second derivative ${V}^{″}(r)$ is

$$
{V}^{″}(r)=\frac{-6\pi r}{2}=-3\pi r,
$$

and we can see that ${V}^{″}(6)<0.$ So, the stationary point $r=6$ is indeed a maximum of $V(r).$

So the cylinder with the largest volume has a radius of $r=6\,\text{in}.$

Finally, to find the largest volume ${V}_{\text{max}},$ we substitute $r=6\,\text{in}$ into the equation for the volume $V:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{max}}=V(6) & =(54(6)-\frac{1}{2}(6)^{3})\pi  \\  & =(324-\frac{216}{2})\pi  \\  & =(324-108)\pi  \\  & =216\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$
